title: [AAFLOW+] Stateful Operator Abstraction with Zero-Copy Distributed KV Cache Orchestration for Multi-Agent Workflows
event_hint: AAFLOW+: distributed KV cache orchestration system for multi-agent LLM workflows with stateful operators
problem: Multi-agent LLM systems remain fundamentally text-centric, requiring agents to repeatedly recompute shared context through expensive prefill operations. KV-cache management is typically restricted to local serving scopes, limiting reuse across distributed agents.
mechanism: AAFLOW+ extends agentic workflow operators to make KV cache a first-class distributed systems object. It builds processes into communication-aware graphs that concurrently optimize data, prompts, and reusable model state. The system provides operators for KV materialization, transfer, fork, composition, and eviction. Runtime enables zero-copy, transfer-aware execution, allowing agents to reuse long context without recomputation. Forked states initially share block references, so memory grows with branch continuation rather than full-context duplication.

evaluation_context: Evaluation uses a trace-driven model parameterized by hardware microbenchmarks on a distributed GPU cluster of 4-16 nodes, each with NVIDIA A100 (80GB/40GB), 32-64 CPU cores, and RDMA-enabled InfiniBand interconnects. Experiments use deterministic synthetic long-context prompts with context lengths from 1K-32K tokens (mean context grid variation), 64 generated output tokens per branch, and agent counts from 1-16. Tested across HuggingFace, vLLM, and SGLang backends with Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 and Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct models. Network configuration: 25 GB/s (200 Gbps) bandwidth, 50μs network latency for main experiments; Experiment 3 sweeps bandwidth from 10-400 Gbps with both RDMA-like (10μs) and Ethernet-like (100μs) latency settings. TTFT measured at 0.041s (Mistral) and 0.030s (Llama3) for AAFLOW+ vs 2.057s and 0.509s for AAFLOW-text baselines. Throughput measured at ~302 tokens/s vs ~31-40 tokens/s for baselines.
limitations: Evaluation methodology uses analytical cost modeling parameterized by hardware microbenchmarks rather than direct end-to-end runtime measurements on live serving infrastructure. Workloads use deterministic synthetic prompts rather than real-world datasets or production workloads. Validation covers only specific backends (HF, vLLM, SGLang) and models (Mistral-7B, Llama3-8B). Output length is fixed at 64 tokens per branch; TTFT advantage would diminish for longer outputs where decode time dominates. Results are projected from a trace-driven model—the aggregate latency values represent modeled workload costs, not observed Slurm wall-clock runtime. Framework overhead Ω is explicitly modeled as 0.0075s for AAFLOW+, distinguishing orchestration cost from compute. P95 latency, tail behavior, and real serving deployment metrics not reported. Network-side mechanisms that actively perceive KV state placement, inference stages, or token performance goals are not introduced—system operates at distributed systems layer rather than network layer.
project_relevance: Directly relevant to TPN's focus on KV-cache-aware network and bandwidth scheduling. The transfer/recomputation scheduler provides concrete decision rules for when KV transmission outperforms recomputation across different bandwidth conditions (10-400 Gbps). At 200 Gbps with RDMA-like latency, KV transfer is beneficial for most tested contexts; at 10 Gbps, transfer remains preferable for 5/8 contexts. However, AAFLOW+ does not introduce network-side mechanisms that actively perceive KV state placement, inference stages, or token performance goals—it operates at the distributed systems layer rather than the network layer. The work demonstrates that moderate-to-high bandwidth networks make KV transmission superior to recomputation, with specific throughput gains (~302 vs ~32 tokens/s, 7.8-9.5× improvement) and TTFT reductions (0.041s vs 2.057s, 50.2× for Mistral). Framework overhead is explicitly modeled at 0.0075s versus 11.17s for text-based passing. The trace-driven modeling approach distinguishes between orchestration overhead and compute cost, but P95 latency, tail behavior, and real serving deployment metrics are not reported.
